details:
Waqaa (وقاء) is a flood-safety concept for wadis (dry valleys) in Saudi Arabia. Many people visit wadis for recreation and judge them by old experience, with no easy way to know whether conditions around a wadi have changed.

What it does: We analysed 24 years (2001–2024) of NASA GPM IMERG daily rainfall (GPM_3IMERGDF v07, downloaded through NASA Giovanni) around two wadis: Wadi Hanifa (Riyadh) and Wadi Bishah (Asir). For each wadi we computed three yearly measures (strongest daily rain, total rain, number of heavy-rain days) and tested each trend with the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s slope, with a correction for multiple tests.

Results: Wadi Hanifa shows no confirmed trend. In Wadi Bishah, total yearly rain is rising by about 4.6 mm per year (p = 0.002), while heavy-rain trends are not confirmed.

Impact and vision: The analysis is the foundation for an early-warning app that tells citizens when to stay away from a wadi, and a dashboard that helps Civil Defense decide when to alert. We designed both screens as prototypes. Next steps are soil moisture (GLDAS), near-real-time rain and terrain.

Tools: Python (pandas, matplotlib) on a MacBook Pro; NASA Giovanni; interface prototype screens.

Creativity: We turn statistics into simple status messages for citizens and a readable dashboard for Civil Defense, and we show “no confirmed trend” honestly instead of raising false alarms.

Limits we considered: satellite rainfall is an estimate and can be less accurate in arid and mountainous terrain; each wadi is represented by one area around a point; trends describe the past and are not a flood forecast.
